bull.b: Growing cloud revenue and a larger share from production applications indicate customers are moving beyond experimentation toward recurring operational use. This supports a more scalable service model, strengthens software and platform engagement, and could improve revenue durability as deployments expand.

Peer-reviewed hardware validation provides external support for D-Wave’s gate-model architecture and complements its established annealing platform. Demonstrated fidelity, error detection, and a multi-year roadmap broaden the potential addressable workload set and support long-term differentiation.

The sharp increase in bookings and remaining performance obligations improves visibility into future revenue and signals stronger commercial traction. Recognition expected over the next two years can support customer expansion, planning, and investment while reducing reliance on entirely new bookings each quarter.

bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow show that the business currently consumes substantial cash to operate rather than funding growth internally. Continued burn can require external financing, constrain strategic flexibility, and increase execution pressure until revenue growth begins covering the cost base.

Widening adjusted EBITDA losses indicate that commercial and product investments are currently outpacing the company’s ability to monetize growth. A heavy cost structure may prolong the path to profitability, consume liquidity, and make future results more sensitive to execution and spending discipline.

The steep first-half revenue decline highlights dependence on irregular system sales and the timing of deliveries and installations. This volatility makes underlying growth harder to assess, can create uneven quarterly results, and leaves near-term performance dependent on successfully completing planned system shipments.
